text.title: Activation Tactics Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every Activation Tactics application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Every tactic in the playbook step MUST name the funnel step it targets, that step's current conversion rate, and the activation event it is meant to move users toward. A tactic with no target step (e.g. "improve onboarding") MUST NOT be included.

rationale.source: Sean Ellis and Morgan Brown, Hacking Growth (2017); widely established growth practice

rule.rationale: Tactics chosen from a list of what other products do land on steps that were never the problem. Binding each tactic to a measured drop-off keeps the work on the step where users are actually lost, and gives the baseline the success check needs.

rule.statement: An activation checklist MUST contain between three and five items, exactly one of which is flagged `activation_event: true`, and that item MUST be `required: true`. Every item MUST resolve either to a navigable `action` path or to a tracked event that checks it automatically; no item may require the user to tick it by hand.

rationale.source: Kivetz, Urminsky and Zheng, 'The Goal-Gradient Hypothesis Resurrected', Journal of Marketing Research (2006); widely established onboarding practice (Appcues, Userpilot guides)

rule.rationale: Progress toward a visible goal accelerates effort, but only while the goal is short: a nine-item checklist reads as work and gets abandoned. Manually ticked items decouple the checklist from behaviour, so "completed" stops meaning "activated".

rule.statement: Each lifecycle email MUST contain exactly one call to action, and that link MUST land on the screen where the targeted action is performed, not on the home page or a login wall. The email body MUST state the expected time to complete the action.
rule.rationale: Two links split intent and the click that matters loses. A link that drops the user on the dashboard adds a navigation step to the very funnel the email exists to shorten, and re-creates the drop-off the tactic targets.

rule.statement: Every email after Day 0 MUST carry a send-time condition `not activated`, evaluated against the activation event at the moment of sending, not at enrolment. The sequence MUST NOT exceed four sends inside the activation window, and the schedule (Day 0 / 1 / 3 / 7 in the template) MUST be stated per email.

rationale.source: widely established lifecycle-messaging practice; CAN-SPAM and GDPR expectations on relevance and frequency

rule.rationale: "Quick win: do this in 5 minutes" sent to a user who did it yesterday is the message that earns the unsubscribe. Enrolment-time evaluation is the usual bug: the user is checked once, then receives all four emails regardless.

rule.statement: Segmented onboarding MAY be used only when the segment key (use case, role, or plan) is captured at signup or from a source available before the first session. Each segment MUST name its own first action and MUST map to the same activation event unless the spec explicitly defines a per-segment event. Segments with no distinct first action MUST be merged.

rationale.source: Hacking Growth (Ellis and Brown); widely established onboarding practice for multi-persona products

rule.rationale: A segment inferred from behaviour arrives after the drop-off it was meant to prevent. Segments that share a first action are a maintenance cost with no activation benefit, and per-segment events without a spec make the activation rate incomparable across segments.

rule.statement: Tooltips and in-app guides MUST be attached to the screen of the targeted drop-off step, at most one active guide per screen, dismissible in one click, and MUST NOT be shown again to a user who has completed the step. A guide MUST NOT be placed on a screen with no measured drop-off.

rationale.source: widely established product-tour practice (Appcues, Pendo, Userpilot documentation); Nielsen Norman Group guidance on instructional overlays

rule.rationale: Guides accumulate: every team adds one, none removes one, and the new user's first screen becomes a stack of dismissals. Placing them only where users are measured to stall, and removing them once the step is done, keeps the guide a fix for a known problem rather than decoration.

rule.statement: The `exit_criterion` of the rollout step for every tactic MUST state the metric (target step conversion or activation rate within the window), its pre-tactic baseline value, and the minimum lift at which the tactic stays. A tactic whose exit criterion is "shipped" or "reviewed" MUST NOT be accepted.

rationale.source: Hacking Growth (Ellis and Brown); Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang and Ya Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments (2020)

rule.rationale: Without a pre-stated threshold every tactic is declared a success by whoever built it, and the onboarding flow accretes checklists, tooltips and emails that each "helped" while the activation rate never moved.

rule.statement: Two tactics targeting the same funnel step MUST NOT run in the same period unless they are arms of one controlled experiment. The `decision_branches` MUST include a branch that defers a tactic when its step already has a live tactic.

rationale.source: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments (Kohavi, Tang and Xu); widely established experimentation practice

rule.rationale: A checklist and a tooltip launched on the same step in the same week produce one number that cannot be attributed to either, so the losing tactic is kept forever alongside the winning one.
